title: Isaiah Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 10.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:1 warn against?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:1 warns 'Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed;' which points to condemning those who make unjust laws.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:2, who are taken advantage of by those who decree unrighteous decrees?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:2 states that the needy are turned aside from judgment so that 'widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 10:3, what is questioned about the day of visitation?
options: To whom will you flee for help?
questions.correctAnswer: To whom will you flee for help?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 asks, 'to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory?' questioning who will aid in the coming desolation.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 10:4 says that without God, people shall bow down under the prisoners and fall under the slain.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:4 clearly states 'Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain.' indicating dependence on God for deliverance.

questions.question: Who is called the rod of God's anger in Isaiah 10:5?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:5 says, 'O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger,' identifying the Assyrian as the instrument of God's wrath.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:6, against whom will God send the Assyrian?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states God will send the Assyrian 'against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 10:7 says the Assyrian intends to destroy many nations.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:7 says, 'it is in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.' confirming the Assyrian's intent to destroy many.

questions.question: What question does the Assyrian king ask in Isaiah 10:8?
options: Are not my princes altogether kings?
Is not the LORD my God?
questions.correctAnswer: Are not my princes altogether kings?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 quotes the Assyrian king asking, 'Are not my princes altogether kings?' displaying his arrogance.

questions.question: Which cities are compared by the Assyrian in Isaiah 10:9?
options: Calno as Carchemish, Hamath as Arpad, Samaria as Damascus
Jerusalem as Babylon, Nineveh as Tyre, Egypt as Ethiopia
Sodom as Gomorrah, Zoar as Admah, Bela as Zoar
Rome as Athens, Corinth as Sparta, Carthage as Alexandria
questions.correctAnswer: Calno as Carchemish, Hamath as Arpad, Samaria as Damascus
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:9 lists these exact comparisons to boast of his conquests.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 10:10 mentions the Assyrian's hand finding kingdoms of idols superior to Jerusalem and Samaria.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:10 says the graven images of the kingdoms found by Assyria excelled those of Jerusalem and Samaria, so the idols were superior, not the kingdoms themselves.

questions.question: What will the LORD do after finishing His work upon mount Zion and Jerusalem according to Isaiah 10:12?
options: Punish the king of Assyria for his pride
Gather the exiles from all nations
questions.correctAnswer: Punish the king of Assyria for his pride
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:12 states the LORD will punish 'the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks.'

questions.question: Which event happens first according to Isaiah 10:1-12?
options: The LORD punishing the king of Assyria
The Assyrian boasting of his conquests
The LORD sending the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned is the decreeing of unrighteous decrees in verse 1 before the LORD's actions against Assyria later in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 10:11 says the LORD will do to Jerusalem and her idols as He did to Samaria and her idols.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:11 affirms that God will do the same to Jerusalem and her idols as He did to Samaria and her idols.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:13 say the Assyrian boasts about?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:13 quotes the Assyrian boasting, 'By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:14, how does the Assyrian describe gathering the riches of the people?
options: Like gathering eggs left in a nest
Like drawing water from a well
questions.correctAnswer: Like gathering eggs left in a nest
questions.explanation: Verse 14 compares the gathering of riches to 'as one gathereth eggs that are left' in a nest, emphasizing ease and thoroughness.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:13, what does the king of Assyria claim about his actions?
options: He did everything by the strength and wisdom of his own hand
He was guided by the LORD in all his conquests
He acted out of mercy and justice
He sought peace among the nations
questions.correctAnswer: He did everything by the strength and wisdom of his own hand
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:13 states the king of Assyria claims, 'By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent.' This shows his pride and self-reliance rather than trust in God (Isaiah 10:12, 10:14).

questions.question: What metaphor does Isaiah 10:14 use to describe how the king of Assyria has gathered the riches of the people?
options: As one gathereth eggs that are left in a nest
As a lion devours its prey
As a farmer harvests his crops
As a fisherman catches fish in a net
questions.correctAnswer: As one gathereth eggs that are left in a nest
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:14 uses the metaphor of gathering eggs left in a nest to describe how the king has taken the remaining riches of the people without resistance (Isaiah 10:13-15).

questions.question: What lesson about pride and dependence does Isaiah 10:15 teach through the comparison of the axe and saw to their users?
options: Tools cannot boast against those who use them, just as humans cannot act against God
The axe and saw are more powerful than their users
The tools have independent power to accomplish work
The king of Assyria is more powerful than his army
questions.correctAnswer: Tools cannot boast against those who use them, just as humans cannot act against God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:15 uses the analogy that the axe cannot boast against him that heweth with it, emphasizing that humans, like tools, are under God's control and cannot act independently against Him (Isaiah 10:13-14).

questions.question: What consequence does Isaiah 10:16 say the Lord will bring upon the 'fat ones'?
options: Leanness and a burning like fire
questions.correctAnswer: Leanness and a burning like fire
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:16 declares that the Lord will send leanness among the fat ones and kindle a burning like fire under their glory, indicating judgment against the proud (Isaiah 10:15-17).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:17, what will the light of Israel and His Holy One do?
options: Burn and devour the thorns and briers in one day
Bring healing and restoration to the land
Lead Israel into peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Burn and devour the thorns and briers in one day
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:17 states that the light of Israel will be a fire and His Holy One a flame that burns and devours the thorns and briers, symbolizing swift purification and judgment (Isaiah 10:16-18).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:18 describe as being consumed by the Lord's judgment?
options: The glory of the forest and fruitful field, both soul and body
Only the wicked leaders of Israel
The cities but not the land
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of the forest and fruitful field, both soul and body
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:18 explains that the Lord's judgment will consume the glory of the forest and fruitful field, both soul and body, indicating comprehensive destruction (Isaiah 10:17-19).

questions.question: How does Isaiah 10:19 illustrate the extent of destruction left in the forest?
options: So few trees remain that a child can write them
Only the tallest trees are left standing
The forest is replaced by a desert
questions.correctAnswer: So few trees remain that a child can write them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:19 uses the image that only a few trees will remain, few enough that a child may write them, showing the severity of devastation (Isaiah 10:18-20).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:20, what will the remnant of Israel do in that day?
options: Stay upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth
Rely on the Assyrian king for protection
Flee to foreign nations for help
Build their own armies for defense
questions.correctAnswer: Stay upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:20 promises that the remnant of Israel will no longer rely on their oppressors but will trust and stay upon the LORD in truth (Isaiah 10:19-21).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:21 say about the remnant of Jacob?
options: They shall return unto the mighty God
They will be scattered among the nations
They will be destroyed by the Assyrians
questions.correctAnswer: They shall return unto the mighty God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:21 declares that the remnant of Jacob will return to the mighty God, signifying repentance and restoration (Isaiah 10:20-22).

questions.question: What hope is given in Isaiah 10:22 despite Israel's multitude?
options: A remnant shall return despite being as numerous as the sand of the sea
All Israel will be lost without hope
The entire nation will be destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: A remnant shall return despite being as numerous as the sand of the sea
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:22 assures that although Israel is as numerous as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return, showing God's sovereign preservation (Isaiah 10:21-23).

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:23 say about the Lord GOD of hosts' plan for the land?
options: He will make a determined consumption in the midst of the land
He will bless the land with peace and prosperity
He will remove all enemies without judgment
He will leave the land untouched
questions.correctAnswer: He will make a determined consumption in the midst of the land
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:23 states that the Lord GOD will execute a determined consumption (judgment) in the land, indicating a decisive act of justice (Isaiah 10:22-24).

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 10:24, how should the people of Zion respond to the Assyrian threat?
options: Be not afraid of the Assyrian
Prepare for endless war without hope
questions.correctAnswer: Be not afraid of the Assyrian
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:24 commands the people of Zion not to fear the Assyrian, despite his threat, because God's judgment will limit the enemy's power (Isaiah 10:23-25).

questions.question: What will happen to the indignation and anger against Israel according to Isaiah 10:25?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:25 promises that after a little while, the indignation and anger against Israel will cease in their destruction, showing God's ultimate mercy (Isaiah 10:24-26).

questions.question: Isaiah 10:26 compares the scourge the LORD will raise up for Assyria to what past event?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:26 compares the scourge against Assyria to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb and to the lifting of a rod over the sea as in Egypt, illustrating a decisive divine judgment (Isaiah 10:25-27).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:27, will the yoke of Assyria remain on Israel forever?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:27 states that in that day, the yoke shall be taken away and destroyed because of the anointing, indicating Israel's liberation from Assyrian oppression (Isaiah 10:26-28).

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10, what will happen to the yoke and burden upon Israel in the day of deliverance?
options: They will be taken away and destroyed
They will be transferred to another nation
questions.correctAnswer: They will be taken away and destroyed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:27 states that the burden will be taken away from the shoulder, the yoke from the neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing.

questions.question: Which historical event is Isaiah 10:26 comparing the LORD's stirring up of a scourge to?
options: The slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb
The crossing of the Jordan River
questions.correctAnswer: The slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:26 parallels God's judgment upon Assyria to the destruction of Midian at the rock of Oreb, a key event recorded in Judges 7.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'after the manner of Egypt' used in Isaiah 10:26 and 10:24?
options: It symbolizes God's deliverance of Israel from bondage
It points to Egypt's military defeat
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's deliverance of Israel from bondage
questions.explanation: The phrase recalls God's power displayed during the Exodus when He used the rod to deliver Israel from Egypt, showing a pattern of divine judgment and deliverance (Isaiah 10:24,26).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:33, what will the LORD of hosts do to the proud and lofty?
options: Hew them down and humble them
questions.correctAnswer: Hew them down and humble them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:33 clearly states the LORD will lop the bough with terror, hewing down the high ones and humbling the haughty.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 10:33-34 where the LORD is described as cutting down the thickets of the forest and Lebanon falling?
questions.explanation: The imagery of cutting down forests and Lebanon falling represents God's judgment on proud nations, a metaphor for destruction and humbling (Isaiah 10:33-34).

questions.question: Which city mentioned in Isaiah 10:29 is described as being afraid due to the Assyrian invasion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:29 states that Ramah is afraid, indicating fear among the cities due to Assyrian military movements.

questions.question: In Isaiah 10:20-21, what is the remnant of Israel instructed to do?
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 emphasize that the remnant of Israel will no longer rely on their oppressors but will stay upon the LORD and return unto the mighty God.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 10:25 promises that God's indignation and anger against Assyria will continue indefinitely.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:25 states 'For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease, and mine anger in their destruction,' indicating that God's anger is temporary.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'yoke' in Isaiah 10:27 metaphorically represent in the context of this chapter?
options: A symbol of hardship and oppression
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of hardship and oppression
questions.explanation: The 'yoke' metaphorically refers to the burden and oppression imposed by Assyria on Israel, which will be removed because of God's anointing (Isaiah 10:27).

questions.question: Which earlier biblical event does Isaiah 10:26 allude to by mentioning the rod lifted 'after the manner of Egypt'?
options: The giving of the Ten Commandments
The parting of the Red Sea during the Exodus
questions.correctAnswer: The parting of the Red Sea during the Exodus
questions.explanation: The reference to the rod lifted 'after the manner of Egypt' evokes God's mighty act in the Exodus when He used His rod to part the Red Sea and defeat Egypt (Exodus 14).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:24, why should the people of Zion not fear the Assyrian?
options: Because the Assyrian will become their ally
Because God's indignation will cease and He will destroy the Assyrian
Because the Assyrian is weaker than Egypt
Because Zion will surrender to the Assyrian
questions.correctAnswer: Because God's indignation will cease and He will destroy the Assyrian
questions.explanation: Verse 25, closely related to 10:24, assures that the indignation will cease and God's anger will end in the destruction of the Assyrian, giving reason not to fear (Isaiah 10:24-25).

questions.question: Which Old Testament book records the event comparable to the 'slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb' mentioned in Isaiah 10:26?
questions.explanation: The slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb is recorded in Judges 7, when Gideon defeated Midianites with God's help, paralleling Isaiah's imagery of divine judgment.

questions.question: In Isaiah 10:28-29, which of these locations is NOT mentioned as being part of the Assyrian military movement?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem is mentioned later as the hill being shaken (Isaiah 10:32), but is not listed among the places where the Assyrians have laid up their carriages or taken lodging in verses 28-29.

questions.question: What theme from Isaiah 10 is echoed in the New Testament book of Romans regarding God's sovereignty and remnant?
options: Romans 9's discussion of God's sovereign election of a remnant
Romans 13's teaching on submission to authorities
Romans 5's explanation of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 9's discussion of God's sovereign election of a remnant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:20-22 speaks of a remnant of Israel returning to God, a theme echoed in Romans 9 where Paul discusses God's sovereign choice and preservation of a faithful remnant.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 10:15 uses a rhetorical question to illustrate the absurdity of the Assyrian king's arrogance.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:15 employs rhetorical questions comparing an axe and saw boasting against the one who wields them, highlighting the folly of the king's pride.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned for those who decree unrighteous decrees according to Isaiah 10:1?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:1 pronounces a woe upon those who decree unrighteous decrees, indicating that they will face consequences for their actions.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:2, what are the poor and needy deprived of?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:2 states that the needy are turned aside from judgment and the rights of the poor are taken away, emphasizing social injustice.

questions.question: What is described as the 'rod of mine anger' in Isaiah 10:5?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:5 identifies the Assyrian as the 'rod of mine anger,' indicating that God is using Assyria as an instrument of judgment.

questions.question: What will happen to the glory of the king of Assyria according to Isaiah 10:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:12 states that the Lord will punish the glory of the king of Assyria for his pride and arrogance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:15 imply about the power of the Assyrian compared to God?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:15 uses the metaphor of an axe and a saw to illustrate that the Assyrian king is merely a tool in God's hands, emphasizing God's sovereignty.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:20, who will the remnant of Israel depend on in the future?
options: The LORD, the Holy One of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD, the Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:20 indicates that the remnant will no longer rely on their oppressors but will trust in the Lord for deliverance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:22 suggest about the number of those who will return?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:22 states that although Israel's people may be numerous, only a remnant will return, indicating God's preservation of a faithful group.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Isaiah 10:16 regarding His judgment?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:16 reveals God's attribute of justice, as He sends leanness among the fat ones, indicating judgment against pride and excess.

questions.question: Which verse indicates that God will take away the burden from the people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:27 promises that in that day, God will remove the burden from their shoulders, symbolizing relief and deliverance from oppression.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:18 say will happen to the glory of Israel's forest?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:18 states that the glory of Israel's forest will be consumed, indicating severe judgment upon the land.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:3 question regarding the day of visitation?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:3 asks the rhetorical question about what will be done in the day of visitation, emphasizing the seriousness of impending judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:24 instruct the people of Zion not to do?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:24 tells the people not to be afraid of the Assyrian, indicating God's assurance of protection despite the threat.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 10:8, what does the Assyrian king claim about his princes?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:8 shows the Assyrian king's pride as he claims that his princes are all kings, reflecting his arrogance and self-importance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:26 reference when speaking of the Lord stirring up a scourge?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:26 alludes to the historical event of the slaughter of Midian, showing that God will act decisively against the Assyrians as He did before.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 10:13 highlight about the Assyrian's perception of his achievements?
options: He believes they are due to his strength
questions.correctAnswer: He believes they are due to his strength
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:13 reveals the Assyrian's pride as he claims to have accomplished his feats by his own strength and wisdom.
